key_insight: Experts perceived an AI mathematics partner as a peer primarily through its social behavior—not its mathematical capabilities.
engineering_relevance: Peer-oriented learning agents should support shared control, tentative reasoning, and learner-paced interaction rather than defaulting to agreement or instruction.
method: Combined a Big Five-informed persona with motivational state modulation in an adaptive LLM agent.
Engaged domain experts in collaborative mathematics problem solving with the agent.
Analyzed expert interviews thematically to identify conditions shaping peer perceptions.
evidence_signal: Expert interviews linked peer perceptions to emotional safety, collaborative reasoning, and appropriate imperfection; blind agreement and over-instruction undermined trust.
watch_item: The abstract reports expert perceptions, not evidence of improved student learning outcomes.
paper_title: Exploring AI Peer in Collaborative Mathematics Learning
